mine_p06_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_001.text: On Day 485, wind lifted the red dust from the outer road and carried it across the receiving yard in long low sheets. Lin wrapped a cloth over her mouth before crossing to her assigned desk. Qiao had moved light paperwork beneath the covered surface bay and kept the empty carts secured. Nobody expected a cultivator to hold the weather still. The practical change made work possible without pretending the day resembled the quiet intervals in the posted plan.

mine_p06_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_002.text: Ren Tao put a stone on the corner of the public board while Lin checked the next deliveries. The stone rolled off when an empty container knocked the table. She caught the loose paper with an ordinary hand and asked for the table to be moved farther from the container lane. Qiao approved the safer placement. The correction took two workers a short interval. Lin resumed with the actual references dry beneath the canopy, noticing how easily a small repeated nuisance could become everyone's accepted working posture.

mine_p06_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_003.text: Deng Huan arrived for his light turn carrying no basket. His clinician's present restriction still excluded lifting the ordinary loads he had once handled. He said people kept offering him small exceptions because each one looked harmless by itself. Qiao reminded the leads to assign the agreed task rather than test his recovery through favors. Lin did not ask whether he felt stronger yet. She asked how the desk's chair fitted his supported arm. He said badly, and they found another permitted seat.

mine_p06_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_004.text: At noon a gust struck the canopy hard enough to interrupt conversation. Fan Luwei examined its ordinary fastenings with the area cleared. One needed replacement before the sheltered bay could keep working. The receiving staff used the inspected alternative, and Lin carried only her own light board as directed. For several minutes the mine's important business consisted of people standing somewhere else. The delay annoyed a driver waiting for a signature. Fan finished the check before the signature process returned to its previous place.

mine_p06_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_005.text: The driver said every journey was being made slower by somebody's precaution. Ren asked which part of the booked receiving interval the delay had changed and entered the actual time. Lin saw the driver's shoulders drop once the complaint had a place. He still disliked waiting. A visible delay did not eliminate his other appointments, but it prevented him needing to exaggerate the wind into a catastrophe before anyone would recognize that his ordinary day had been affected.

mine_p06_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_006.text: After her half-day, Lin walked to the lodging lane with dust inside the fold of her cuff. The conducting stitch remained sound, and she cleaned it without activating it. A windy yard could contaminate ordinary equipment while leaving her stage unchanged. She hung the cloth outside and ate before opening the incoming papers. The agreements which had brought her to the mine no longer belonged at the center of every conversation. Their actual remaining obligations needed an end, rather than gradual disappearance beneath more interesting work.

mine_p06_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_007.text: Qiao had scheduled a closing appointment for the incoming role and its source holders. The meeting was not an offer to renew every permission. A completed receiving task could leave an unresolved cargo disposition, an open instrument return, or people whose next independent arrangements had begun. Lin brought the papers which actually concerned her. Her own pack required no transfer. Any retained source copy would stay within its original allowed use after the role ended.

mine_p06_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_008.text: The yard had begun to feel familiar enough that leaving an agreement unsettled seemed less urgent than it had on arrival. Lin understood the danger in that comfort. A borrowed kit could sit in a cupboard until everyone began to treat it as mine equipment. A temporary board arrangement could look permanent once a person learned the path to the kitchen. She wrote the remaining end conditions on a clean page and left space for actual outcomes instead of crossing them out because the mine had stopped feeling new.

mine_p06_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_009.text: Han Bo asked whether the closing appointment meant she was leaving. Lin said her current surface-work agreement remained, and she was considering a separate human cultivation curriculum. Han looked at her room key and said the bed would still be an ordinary bed if she advanced. She laughed, then realized she had been imagining the next stage as a border beyond familiar problems. The keeper's roof, her board payment and the mended boots would require the same attention afterward.

mine_p06_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_010.text: On Day 486, she passed Zeng Bo carrying a customer's stool toward the surface workshop. The repaired hammer stayed in his tool roll. He complained about the wind depositing dust on a freshly fitted joint, then asked whether Lin knew a clean place to wait. She pointed to the public sheltered standing place approved after the canopy repair. He went there with the stool. His property problem had not ended the world's smaller inconveniences, and his ordinary work no longer needed every conversation to begin with the hammer's hold.

mine_p06_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_011.text: Lei An was cleaning lamp-store cloths when Lin returned for supper. He had folded the observation drawing copies Jia permitted him to keep and wanted to know what would happen to them when the moth survey changed. Lin said they would remain dated records, not turn into the latest finding by staying on the shelf. Lei pinned one beside a child's drawing of a grey bun with wings. They could look at both without confusing their purposes. The household wall did not need to become a formal field archive.

mine_return_gate.speaker: narrator
mine_return_gate.text: The closing appointment began at the surface office the next morning. Ren checked the actual incoming selection against its allowed task and the papers present. If a role was not supported by a record, Lin would not claim its cargo, testimony, equipment or payment. She could still complete her own current work and seek new permission through the ordinary process. Qiao asked which source holder needed a final answer. Lin opened the relevant packet, ready to let a finished agreement stay finished.

mine_p06_convoy_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_convoy_001.text: The convoy packet concerned the six port-owned crates of freight-signal plates. Lin's receiving work had ended on Day 443 and its ten-copper wage had been paid then. Sui Jun brought the owner's permitted public disposition for the one plate held after the comparison. The ordinary repair had now been completed under a separate owner-approved arrangement. The qualified comparator had checked it afterward. Lin saw the difference between learning that work had finished and claiming to have performed it because she had been present at its earlier problem.

mine_p06_convoy_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_convoy_002.text: Sui laid the plate's public condition reference beside the original crate number. The port representative accepted the actual repair disposition on Day 487. The repaired item remained port property and would enter the owner's intended service only under its stated ordinary rating. Lin was not offered the pale replaced strip as a souvenir. The crate's condition history stayed with the receiving account, including the initial unresolved finding. Completion did not require a cleaner story about how perfectly the convoy had arrived.

mine_p06_convoy_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_convoy_003.text: The licensed carrier's twenty-four-copper receipt, packing four, message service four, Lin's four-day arrival board eight and completed receiving wage ten accounted for the fifty-copper freight fund. No balance remained for a new laboratory visit or personal practice. Ren closed that account with its actual receipts. Lin retained the public copies allowed by the agreement. Sui kept the detailed private comparison sources. The book's final line identified what had closed, not a broad declaration that every question involving the supplier was over.

mine_p06_convoy_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_convoy_004.text: At the cargo bay, the port representative examined the repaired plate before accepting the ordinary transfer to its service carrier. His name was Shen Du. He had spent the previous night on the road and wanted the check done quickly enough to leave before another weather interval. The comparator kept the required sequence. Shen waited, rubbing his cold hands. Lin did not mistake his impatience for knowledge that the check was unnecessary. The delay left the plate's accepted condition visible instead of replacing it with somebody's confidence.

mine_p06_convoy_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_convoy_005.text: One packing worker found the old shifted strip beneath a tray and asked if it should travel with the plate. Shen wanted it retained with the condition source, not tucked into the new working packing. The worker labelled it through the proper holder and kept the service packing clear. Lin watched a small damaged piece receive a purpose which was neither secret salvage nor rubbish by default. Its ordinary presence would explain an earlier condition if the owner later needed to examine the account.

mine_p06_convoy_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_convoy_006.text: Sui invited Lin to the public closing table because her permitted receiving references were part of the completed sequence. The original supplier bench reservation had already ended after the defined comparison. A new independent cultivation curriculum would need another place and another accepted arrangement. Lin asked whether Sui knew the local booking route for such a place. He named the public practice-court steward and made no promise on the steward's behalf. She wrote the contact in her own notebook, not inside the freight account.

mine_p06_convoy_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_convoy_007.text: Shen asked why a cultivator had done ordinary copying for the convoy. Lin said the copying had been needed and she could do it within its terms. He said his office employed people who thought that work beneath them until an incorrectly copied number kept a shipment in a yard. The comment amused her and made her defensive. She had wanted the receiving role to be useful without becoming all she could hope to do. Ordinary competence did not require her to surrender ambition, and ambition did not diminish the finished task.

mine_p06_convoy_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_convoy_008.text: The final public disposition copy contained the crate numbers, receiving dates and accepted condition status. It did not contain the private method for the plate's comparison. Lin checked the copy before signing its issue line. She could keep it after the role closed for the use its owner allowed. She could not carry it to a different employer as a complete freight method or appoint herself to explain the port's plans. The narrower paper was still useful because it said what she had actually helped receive.

mine_p06_convoy_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_convoy_009.text: On Day 490, the service carrier took the accepted cargo under the port owner's instruction. Ordinary workers secured the numbered crates for the actual journey. Lin stood clear of the load path while the driver checked the fastenings. She was not needed to lend qi to a task planned for timber, rope and trained people. The cart moved through the gate slowly enough for a child to become bored watching it. Lin liked that unheroic speed. An expensive cargo could leave safely without turning departure into a personal display.

mine_p06_convoy_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_convoy_010.text: The sound of the wheels lingered after the crates disappeared down the red road. Sui folded the completed receiving sheet and said the bay would be needed for another owner's ordinary goods tomorrow. Lin felt unexpectedly sad at the empty space. She had followed six crate numbers long enough for them to become part of how she knew the yard. Their departure did not remove her own work. It removed a borrowed focus she could now let go without keeping a plate to prove the journey had mattered.

mine_p06_convoy_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_convoy_011.text: That evening she told Lei about the ordinary cart leaving, using only the allowed public details. Lei asked if the repaired piece worked. Lin said it had passed the actual accepted comparison and would serve within the owner's stated rating. Lei said that sounded less thrilling than a magical freight plate and much more likely to keep somebody's supper arriving on time. They finished their own supper while a different carrier's bell sounded below. The mine's commerce continued through work which never needed to become Lin's property.

mine_p06_convoy_012.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_convoy_012.text: At the closing desk Lin signed only her own completed-role acknowledgment. The account's actual source holders closed their parts separately. She kept the wage receipt already paid and the public disposition copy she was allowed to retain. No supplier instrument, bench right, cargo plate or private appendix left in her pack. The convoy had altered her first access to the mine and brought people she might meet again. Its authority ended at its own scope, leaving the next human practice question to be asked afresh.

mine_p06_refuge_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_001.text: The relocation account had closed through eighty-eight coppers spent and four returned after the three accepted optional statements. Lin's two receiving days and ten-copper wage were complete. The arrival tickets and four-day board had not promised employment beyond that period. Ren kept the closure reference ready while the five adults decided their next arrangements. The closing appointment concerned whether each had received the actual agreed arrival service and source conditions, not whether every person had become a useful mine witness.

mine_p06_refuge_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_002.text: Bai Fen had chosen a local tile-repair applicant appointment. Qiao's ordinary crew offered a short accepted turn on a surface roof after checking her relevant experience. It was a new employment agreement with its own lead, hours and pay. Lin saw Bai read the work boundary before signing. She had traveled under relocation terms and now accepted work by another route. The distinction mattered most to Bai, who did not want the journey's kindness described later as a debt she had repaid through labor.

mine_p06_refuge_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_003.text: On Day 488, Bai worked from the inspected ordinary position under the crew lead. Lin passed below while returning to her own surface desk and saw her pause until the scaffold check was complete. Bai's skill did not make the support optional. Later she said the local tile shapes differed from those she knew and she had asked for the fitting pattern before beginning. The new job gave her wages and a place among the crew. It did not grant effortless mastery of every roof in the red mountain settlement.

mine_p06_refuge_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_004.text: Pei Lu had chosen the independent market kitchen instead of the mine's posted applicant turn. The kitchen owner accepted a trial under a stated ordinary agreement after observing her work. Pei would be paid for the accepted hours; the employer did not receive her private port account as part of hiring. Lin visited for a bowl of soup and found her arguing cheerfully about the order in which cabbage should enter the pot. It was a dispute belonging to her new work, unrelated to whether she had once offered a statement.

mine_p06_refuge_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_005.text: The soup tasted sharper than Han's version. Pei blamed the vinegar and then admitted she had added it herself. The kitchen owner laughed and asked her to keep the next pot nearer the agreed recipe. Lin paid for her meal and did not receive a free bowl by virtue of accompanying Pei on the road. The transaction made their conversation easier. Pei could be a friend and a worker whose food had a price, rather than another person expected to perform gratitude for a receiving role now finished.

mine_p06_refuge_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_006.text: Yan He found basket-repair customers through the surface market. He did not accept a mine position. The first customer wanted him to promise a cracked carrying frame could hold its old heavy load after a cheap repair. Yan declined that promise and offered a suitable lighter-use repair or replacement estimate. Lin heard the permitted public conversation while buying thread nearby. He had begun a livelihood through his own ordinary judgment, not through testimony he had declined to give or employment Lin had secretly arranged.

mine_p06_refuge_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_007.text: Xu Zhen followed Chen Ai's advice to reduce carrying while his longstanding shoulder complaint was assessed and managed. He paid the ordinary appointment from his own saved port wages and accepted a bounded lodging arrangement with a consenting cousin. The cousin's help was not part of the ninety-two-copper journey account. Xu declined the mine's porter application for now. Lin asked whether he wanted any receiving paper carried to the clinic. He said no; the clinician had his actual history, and a travel statement would not treat the shoulder.

mine_p06_refuge_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_008.text: His refusal of porter work worried him. He had always expected the next job to require his body before his handwriting. Lin stayed beside him at the surface notice shelter while he read lighter openings. None was promised. He decided to ask about one ordinary counting trial after his next assessment, if its duties matched the clinician's restriction. The plan gave him a possible next step without announcing recovery in advance. Lin wished him a useful appointment and left the choice with him.

mine_p06_refuge_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_009.text: Jin Shu hired a wheel through a local spinner's ordinary arrangement and began work for customers who accepted its actual pace and quality. The hire had an end date and a condition record separate from relocation board. She showed Lin the first finished skein when they met at the market. It was uneven enough that she would sell it for the agreed lesser grade. She looked proud anyway. A new place did not have to turn every first product into either a miracle or a humiliating failure.

mine_p06_refuge_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_010.text: The five adults met the host liaison separately before the final arrival closure. Each confirmed the services actually received and the limits still governing any retained statement. Bai's named work-time account, Pei's restricted observations and Jin's short boarding account remained different sources. Yan and Xu had declined the optional statements, and their board had remained unconditional. Lin did not gather all five around a table to ask them to approve one flattering description of the journey. Their actual answers reached the closing record individually.

mine_p06_refuge_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_011.text: On Day 491, the unused four statement coppers were confirmed back with the journey custodian under the earlier return receipt. The eight arrival-board coppers for Lin and forty for the five adults had paid the accepted four days only. The road tickets had cost twenty-four, her completed receiving work ten, and the three optional intervals six. Ninety-two had therefore become eighty-eight in real services and work plus four actually returned. The source account did not follow anyone into later housing, clinic care or a new employer's budget.

mine_p06_refuge_012.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_012.text: The adults began keeping their own schedules, and Lin stopped seeing them all on the same day. Bai worked with the tile crew; Pei's kitchen interval ended later than her mine desk; Yan met customers; Xu had care and rest to arrange; Jin followed the wheel hire. Their absence from a group table was not evidence that the relocation had failed. It meant arrival had become several lives. Lin felt relieved and a little lonely when a familiar face passed with only a quick greeting.

mine_p06_refuge_013.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_013.text: At the market, Pei told Lin she might eventually travel on again. The statement came while she was chopping onions, without asking permission from the person who had accompanied her uphill. Lin said she hoped the next place would serve better vinegar. Pei laughed and sent her to the customer side of the counter. A possible onward journey did not invalidate the work already done there. The relocation role had brought a consenting adult to a place where she could decide to remain, work, rest or leave.

mine_p06_refuge_014.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_refuge_014.text: Lin closed her own receiving acknowledgment without taking custody of anyone's private statement originals. The host liaison retained the sources under their individual terms. Her pack held her actual allowed references and her own notes. No supplier bench, instrument kit or collective right to speak for five adults had accompanied this role. It had given her conversations which might continue if the participants wanted them. The next inquiry would require a new question addressed to each living person, not another use of a journey whose contract had ended.

mine_p06_survey_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_survey_001.text: The survey loan remained open because the lender-owned kit had not yet passed into authorized return custody. Its deadline was Day 500, and the booked return handover stood on Day 496. The loan named the Outer Shoal Pilots' Association and allowed return to its authorized licensed carrier at the mine under a condition receipt. The subsequent road journey remained the carrier's actual duty. Lin checked that clause with Ren instead of imagining the instruments could reach the distant association in four days because a convenient date had been written in her notebook.

mine_p06_survey_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_survey_002.text: The licensed return service was Lantern Road Carriers. Its named receiver, Tang Lu, carried the association's authorized receiving instruction and the ordinary route booking. The onward journey was booked for fifteen travel days, subject to actual road conditions. Accepting the kit at Vermilion Hollows would end Lin's loan custody under the stated terms. It would not mean the tools had already arrived at the association's distant store. The receipt would identify both facts so a later reader could follow a real parcel rather than a magical shortening of distance.

mine_p06_survey_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_survey_003.text: On Day 487, Lin made the last proposed ordinary issue request under the permitted surface comparison scope. The responsible holder supplied the unpowered level, plumb and marked comparison pieces against their condition list. She used them only with the local lead at the cleared reference. The weather made one planned observation unsuitable, and they stopped that part rather than spend the final loan days forcing a result. A return deadline could encourage haste. It did not make a wet support or unreadable marker an acceptable reference.

mine_p06_survey_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_survey_004.text: They completed the usable portion of the surface comparison and retained the incomplete question clearly. Lin's personal note would describe which placement worked, which had been stopped and why. The authorized public extract remained a source from its named location and date. Nothing in the last issue made it evidence of present mine water or an internal human route. She returned the instruments to their appointed custody that same day, ready for the final condition check before dispatch.

mine_p06_survey_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_survey_005.text: A worker asked to borrow the comparison pieces while the case waited for Tang. Lin referred him to the actual lender scope and mine tool issuer. The proposed task did not fit the loan, and the mine could issue a proper ordinary alternative if available. The worker said he had only hoped to avoid another walk. Lin understood the wish after several weeks of red dust on the lane. A borrowed kit's last evening was not a free interval in which all unaccepted uses could occur without entering its history.

mine_p06_survey_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_survey_006.text: On Day 495, the responsible holder opened the case for the return comparison. Lin was present with the original issue list. The wooden corner chip and plumb-cord fray matched their recorded condition. The level face remained legible, and the marked comparison pieces matched the list. They did not polish wear into the appearance of new tools. Tang would need an accurate condition receipt, including the ordinary marks the lender had already accepted at issue.

mine_p06_survey_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_survey_007.text: The case's packing cloth had collected red dust. Lin cleaned it in the ordinary permitted way and let it dry before wrapping the instruments. She had done enough manual work to know that a hurried damp case could become another owner's later problem. The task took an afternoon outside her mine half-day. She did not bill it as a third incoming receiving day. Her original ten-copper role was already complete, and returning what she had borrowed remained part of the accepted loan rather than an endlessly renewable wage.

mine_p06_survey_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_survey_008.text: Tang arrived on Day 496 with the contracted cart and the association's return authority. Ren compared his name and instruction with the booking before the case crossed the table. Tang checked the listed condition in Lin's presence and accepted custody under the lender-authorized receipt. Four coppers paid the agreed kit-return dispatch service. The case would travel by the booked ordinary road. Lin had not returned its contents to an unseen distant shelf; she had returned them to the authorized holder named in the actual loan.

mine_p06_survey_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_survey_009.text: The fifty-copper survey account could now close: twenty-four for shared transport and seat, eight for arrival board, four for the permitted copy set, ten for Lin's two performed receiving days, and four for actual return dispatch. No balance remained. The permitted public extract and Lin's own nonconfidential observations were hers to retain within their allowed uses. The unpowered instruments remained association property in Tang's custody. Their absence from the cupboard was a real change, not an inconvenience she could undo by claiming another issue after the loan ended.

mine_p06_survey_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_survey_010.text: Tang asked whether she wanted to send a private message with the case. Lin considered the offer and declined because the dispatch agreement covered the named parcel and source papers. She could arrange another ordinary message if she wanted one. Tang secured the case where it would not share loose space with an axle tool. The cart's first movement was slow over the yard stones. Lin watched until the wheels reached the outer road, feeling a small emptiness where the overdue possibility of borrowed equipment had been.

mine_p06_survey_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_survey_011.text: The association's later physical receipt would belong to the carrier's onward record and actual acknowledgment after travel. Lin kept her return-custody receipt, which dated her completed responsibility at the mine. Ren did not close the carrier's journey in his own notebook. A parcel could leave one person's custody while another person's duty continued. The distinction let Lin begin a new curriculum without pretending the tools had traveled faster than people, carts and the road could actually move.

mine_p06_survey_012.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_survey_012.text: That night she reread her permitted public extract and noticed how different it felt without the kit nearby. The words had not changed. The temptation to make every future comparison fit the borrowed instruments had. She would need a new appropriate place and actual rated equipment for human bridge practice, supplied under another accepted arrangement. Lin closed the extract and opened her own question list. A finished loan could leave useful knowledge behind without leaving its owner's tools, field method or authority inside her pack.

mine_p06_after_001.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_001.text: By Day 500, Lin had separated her current mine employment from the incoming agreements and their actual closing records. Lin's common mine employment continued under its own agreement. She had not become the representative of every owner or worker who had entered the yard beside her. The forewoman no longer referred to the incoming role when issuing ordinary desk tasks. She named the current task, lead and interval. Lin felt more settled when her work could be described without retelling the journey.

mine_p06_after_002.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_002.text: The surface garden had new shoots along the repaired drain. Jia Wen retained the current habitat survey, with the additional contribution Lin had actually chosen recorded in its own place. Lin passed the grey moths on the ordinary path and did not interpret every sighting as a demand to reopen that role. The living creatures remained interesting. Her human curriculum now needed questions which had waited through arrival, work and somebody else's tool dispute. Curiosity could move toward another subject without declaring the colony a discarded stage of her own growth.

mine_p06_after_003.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_003.text: When Qiao first gave her the public practice-court contact on Day 485, Lin had begun looking at the terms. The court stood above the haul route in a dry cleared place with a grounded release arrangement and an ordinary physical exit. Booking it would not include all fuel or instruction. She had read the rates and checked her actual paid-wage reserve. Five weeks of two completed half-days had then produced forty coppers gross; twenty had paid the agreed five weeks of board. The actual remainder had been twenty, short of the curriculum package she was considering.

mine_p06_after_004.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_004.text: She could have used other money already in her own purse. She had chosen to wait until the initial eight-week work block had actually earned enough while keeping travel and emergency money separate. The projected remainder of thirty-two would cover a twenty-four-copper bounded curriculum if the remaining work was performed and the stated terms accepted. Projection still was not payment. Lin booked only the public information appointment on Day 505, which did not require pretending the future balance was already inside the folded wage cloth.

mine_p06_after_005.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_005.text: The independent examiner's name was Wei Yan. Her public listing identified the local method, permitted assessment work and interests she would disclose before agreeing to a candidate's curriculum. The mine did not employ her. Lin wrote down the questions she wanted answered about interruption, failed attempts, actual recovery and whether a supplier's equipment could alter the comparison. She had waited long enough to feel impatient with the page. Waiting did not entitle her to a certificate, but it made the unanswered questions feel personal rather than theoretical.

mine_p06_after_006.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_006.text: Lei An asked what the seventh stage would let her do differently. Lin said a stable small circuit would require actual closure through the governing and conception preparation, with the conditions and limits demonstrated rather than assumed. She did not promise a new body which would never tire. Lei listened and said he hoped the circuit would at least improve Lin's talent for choosing a chair which did not wobble. Lin said that remained an ordinary inspection problem. They checked the chair before laughing at it again.

mine_p06_after_007.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_007.text: Deng Huan heard about the curriculum appointment and asked whether Lin could bring back a technique for his shoulder. She said her intended examination concerned her own trained routes and was not a human healing qualification. He looked disappointed for a moment, then said his clinician had warned him against paying for another person's confidence. Lin asked how the current light duty was working. He said better now that the seat fitted. The useful improvement was already present and ordinary, while the harder recovery continued at its own pace.

mine_p06_after_008.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_008.text: The court steward, Guan Si, met her during the public information interval. He swept dust from the doorway while explaining where candidates could wait and who controlled the test places. Lin asked to see the ordinary exit before discussing a booking. Guan pointed to the dry path leading back toward the surface road. He did not make the question sound timid. A practice place which depended on a candidate remaining inside through distress would be a bad place to test whether stopping actually worked.

mine_p06_after_009.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_009.text: At the waiting bench, another learner was mending a tie on an old practice sleeve. Her name was Mu Ran. She had postponed a comparison after sleeping badly and seemed angry with herself for doing so. Lin asked whether the postponement had damaged the booking. Mu said the terms allowed it within the accepted schedule. The anger belonged to wanting the result sooner, not to a new charge. Lin recognized that feeling and sat with her until Guan called the next ordinary inquiry.

mine_p06_after_010.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_010.text: Mu had worked for months toward one primary-route correction and disliked hearing visitors ask which realm came next. She wanted the present task to stop pulling at her wrist. Lin said she had come with similar questions about a future bridge. Their conversation did not exchange techniques. It made the waiting bench less lonely. Another person's careful correction could be important even when it would not produce the stage label Lin herself hoped to earn.

mine_p06_after_011.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_011.text: At the court gate, Mu Ran asked whether Lin would still come back if the examiner refused her first attempt. Lin said she wanted to be able to. The answer surprised them both by sounding like a financial plan as much as a declaration of courage.

mine_p06_after_012.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_012.text: Chen Rui arrived at the mine carrying a client appointment and a folder whose fastening had come loose. He introduced the immediate purpose as contracted advocacy concerning a proposed method comparison. He was not the mine owner. Lin knew his work depended on people agreeing to use an account he prepared, and he had his own interests in the result. When a gust scattered one blank sheet, she helped retrieve it before asking what new work he actually wanted to discuss.

mine_p06_after_013.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_013.text: He said a company client might eventually request observations from a candidate's ordinary tests. Lin said her curriculum and independent examiner had not yet been agreed. He accepted a later conversation instead of collecting advance consent. The postponement disappointed him. He had arrived hoping a practical introduction would shorten several appointments. Lin watched him repair the folder fastening with ordinary cord and thought a fallible advocate could understand delay intimately while still wishing another person's decision would remove it for him.

mine_p06_after_014.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_014.text: That evening she considered his proposed future work more than she wanted to admit. Paid comparison might help fund practice, and the company might prefer a candidate whose route remained convenient. Chen had not promised either outcome. The interests could become harder to distinguish once money and failure entered the same room. Lin added a question about outside use of candidate records to the independent appointment. It would be easier to ask before anybody's favorable result made caution feel disloyal.

mine_p06_after_015.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_015.text: Fu Jie brought a corrected combined-bundle sheet to Lin's normal surface desk on her next half-day. The destination and owner fields now stood far enough apart to read without guessing. He asked her to check the public copy against the issued original. She found no discrepancy in that particular comparison. He looked relieved and then continued to the next bundle. Better work had not made him immune to error. It had given the next task a check which existed before an owner came shouting for a tool.

mine_p06_after_016.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_016.text: On her free afternoon Lin washed the red dust from the hem of her coat. The water took its color slowly, and two rinses were needed. She had imagined long cultivation study as a life of rare materials and decisive mornings. Much of the actual preparation involved keeping ordinary cloth, sleep and meals usable across repeated days. The thought disappointed her and steadied her. A body lived through the intervals between important tests; those intervals would eventually enter the results whether she had paid attention to them or not.

mine_p06_after_017.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_017.text: Han put the next week's board notice beside the lamp where she would see it before leaving for work. Lin thanked him and paid when the agreed day came, using actual wages received rather than the projected final block. He marked the payment and returned to his kitchen. Her future ambition had not become his credit obligation. The ordinary settlement made the room feel secure enough to study in, without requiring the keeper to believe that a small circuit would soon transform his guest into somebody beyond bills.

mine_p06_after_018.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_018.text: Before the information appointment, she checked the practice notebook for questions copied from other people's observations. The moth field, freight comparison and human routes belonged to different methods and purposes. She crossed out a phrase which made external compatibility sound like a human result and kept the underlying question. The correction was small and private. It mattered because she would otherwise bring an attractive confusion to an examiner and ask the examiner to turn it into a plan.

mine_p06_after_019.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_019.text: On the last evening before the information appointment, Lin walked past the surface memorial. Lu Sen's name remained on the board. The authorized song might later provide a bounded source for a different inquiry, and no copied sound could make him attend her examination. She thought of Zeng's father and the broken handle kept beside a window. People carried what could be carried. The new stage she wanted would not settle every loss which had taught her to want more power.

mine_p06_after_020.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_020.text: The mine lamps lit one by one along their ordinary maintained routes. Lin watched an attendant replace a damaged wick and close the housing properly. The small act left the light useful for the next shift. She hoped her own eventual circuit would be as accountable: a specific route, a known input, a release which worked when another task interrupted it. The hope did not make the route available. She would have to learn and test what the living body could actually sustain.

mine_p06_after_021.speaker: narrator
mine_p06_after_021.text: At Han's room table, she placed the ended incoming papers behind their completed references and brought the human practice notebook forward. The old role had changed how she arrived and whom she knew. It did not grant equipment or consent to the next subject. Lin set her question list where morning light would reach it, then put the room key beside the bed. Ordinary sleep came before the appointment. When the courtyard opened, she wanted to bring a rested candidate instead of a story about how badly she deserved an advance.
